chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to pray the two rak'ahs at the Station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) during the tawaf of Hajj and Umrah. He said: 'If he is in the city, he should pray the two rak'ahs at the Station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), for indeed Allah, Exalted and Glorious, says: "And take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer." And if he has already departed, I do not command him to return.'.

Thus, what this report contains of his saying (peace be upon him) 'and I do not command him to return to it' is to be understood as referring to one for whom it is difficult and who is unable to do so. And likewise what is narrated in this meaning that he prays wherever he remembers, is to be understood as what we mentioned. Among that is what he narrated:

key_terms.مَقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Station of Ibrahim (a specific spot in the Masjid al-Haram)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to pray at Maqam Ibrahim during tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the ruling for the two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim, distinguishing between the obligation to return if one is still in Mecca and the concession (*rukhsa*) if one has already departed, which Shia scholars interpret as applying to those for whom returning is burdensome. The Imam grounds this in the Quranic command 'Take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer,' highlighting the spiritual significance of this specific location in Hajj rituals. This ruling reflects the Shia principle of balancing strict adherence to ritual completeness with practical ease for the pilgrim.
